title: Postdoctoral Fellowships in Computational Biology  - Houston, Texas (US) job with The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center | 12862160
gist: A Nature Careers job posting rather than an article: MD Anderson's Cancer Genomics and Evolution Laboratory under Peter Van Loo is hiring computational-biology postdocs in Houston for large-scale pan-cancer genomics and tumor-evolution work. The usable signal is the lab's self-description as mostly computational with a small wet-lab component, 22 Nature/Cell/Science papers since inception, and named research fronts spanning intra-tumor heterogeneity, subclonal reconstruction benchmarking and chromosomal instability in genome-doubled tumors.

insights.claim: The Cancer Genomics and Evolution Laboratory of Peter Van Loo in the Department of Genetics at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center is recruiting postdocs in Houston to spearhead large-scale pan-cancer genomics and tumor-evolution projects, with applications closing 27 Oct 2026.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Tracks where cancer-genomics talent and project funding are concentrating in US academia.
insights.locator: Cancer Genomics and Evolution Laboratory, Prof. Dr. Peter Van Loo

insights.claim: The group describes itself as mostly computational with only a small wet-lab component, centered on large-scale pan-cancer data analysis and on developing computational methods that enable conceptually novel analyses.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Confirms leading cancer-genomics output is now a compute-and-methods business rather than a bench business.
insights.quote: The research group is mostly computational with a small wet-lab component.
insights.locator: The Cancer Genomics and Evolution laboratory

themes.theme: Publication record and active research fronts

insights.claim: Members of the lab have co-authored 22 papers in Nature, Cell or Science since its inception, a publication density that marks where high-impact cancer-genomics output is being produced.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A concrete quality proxy when mapping which academic groups feed biotech IP and founders.
insights.locator: Since its inception, members of the Cancer Genomics and Evolution laboratory

insights.claim: Named recent output marks the field's active fronts: intra-tumor heterogeneity across cancers (Dentro, Cell 2021), the evolutionary history of cancer (Gerstung, Nature 2020), biallelic mutations in cancer genomes (Demeulemeester, Nature Genetics 2022), combined DNA methylation and genomic alterations in lung cancer evolution (Gimeno-Valiente, Nature Genetics 2025), benchmarking of subclonal reconstruction methods (Salcedo, Nature Biotechnology 2025) and chromosomal instability in genome-doubled tumors (Baker, Cancer Discovery 2024).
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Subclonal reconstruction benchmarking and methylation-plus-genomics evolution are the method layers likeliest to reach diagnostics first.
insights.locator: Recent successes include studies of intra-tumor heterogeneity

themes.theme: Skills the field is bidding for

insights.claim: The posting asks for a PhD in computational biology with a proven publication record while explicitly welcoming physicists, (bio)statisticians, biologists and clinicians, and counts prior experience with massively parallel sequencing data as an advantage.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Cancer genomics is bidding for generic quantitative talent, putting it in direct competition with tech and finance for the same hires.
